classification: single-factor substitution in the C sleeve of the R344 extended-window portfolio; intraday/overnight volatility composition
diagnostics: Report the 2022 partial return and drawdown versus R344 control
Report 5x top1/top3/top5 net contribution versus R344 control
Report C standalone return and drawdown as diagnostic only; portfolio gates remain authoritative
Report factor contribution and holdings overlap with the control C sleeve
discipline: One factor substitution only; no parameter scan of the volatility window, ratio definition or risk-budget rules
No paper target or order file
Use historical membership, T+1 open execution and the system StrategyBacktestService
The 20-day intraday/overnight split is frozen before returns; do not tune the window or denominator after results
disclosure: The factor and strategy files were written before any portfolio return, drawdown, trade or concentration result was computed. The coverage-only preflight inspected factor coverage and cross-sectional correlations only. The 2022-05-05 start is inherited from R344 earliest common C-sleeve window. This is a quasi-out-of-sample temporal extension, not an independent 2018-2026 sample.
economic_rationale: The factor is the 20-day realized volatility of intraday returns divided by the sum of 20-day intraday and overnight realized volatility. High values mean less of the stock risk is realized as unhedgeable overnight gaps. The candidate-only mean daily Spearman correlation with the old low-vol leg is -0.0108, with the retained C quality leg -0.0092, with momentum -0.0254, and with Merton DD -0.0344; maximum mean absolute correlation with any comparator is 0.0344.

hypothesis: Replacing the C sleeve generic 15% low-volatility leg with an industry-neutral 15% intraday-risk-share leg improves the 2022 weak-market tail and net-of-5x-cost breadth without materially degrading long-window return or drawdown.
known_limitations: Open/previous-close returns use adjusted prices and can include corporate-action effects if the adjustment factor is stale.
The 20-day volatility decomposition is a statistical risk proxy, not a structural model of information flow.
Financial firms are handled by within-industry neutralization rather than separate treatment.
Current-snapshot industry classification is backfilled through history.
Membership is reconstructed and ETF qfq is not official PIT total return.
The common window starts in 2022 because TTM financial factors are unavailable earlier.
The 10% C cap, broad C design and gold trend rule were selected in prior post-hoc research.

reference_control.use: fixed comparison construction; R344 remains a failed/no-candidate result and is not relabelled

selection_rule: All D/G/T/X/C/R/F/P gates must pass. Otherwise record the result as research-only negative evidence and do not promote or generate paper targets. No threshold, weight, cap or window changes after results.

added_component.interpretation: high intraday realized-volatility share means lower overnight gap-risk share; only backward-looking 20-day daily bars are used
added_component.neutralization: industry_l1 demean plus within-industry z-score; all other scoring legs are excluded from neutralization

single_mutation.control: R344 extended-window construction with C = ai_hs300_quality_momentum_broad_h60
unchanged: monthly A/B/C inverse-volatility risk parity with [0.20, 0.60] bounds
